context: term-date driven · life-safety & IT/AV pace occupancy

brief.intro: New to this project type? A school is a moderate-MEP teaching building whose defining constraint isn't technical complexity — it's a fixed calendar date. There is no big commissioning test like a power plant or data centre; the real schedule risk is that many parallel finishing and fit-out fronts (classrooms, labs, halls, canteen, sports areas) all have to close out life-safety and IT/AV sign-off by one immovable date: the start of the academic term. Because classrooms and labs repeat many times over, treat the internal fit-out like a repetitive typical-floor cycle, not a series of one-off rooms. Order long-lead classroom furniture, AV equipment and specialist lab fixtures early — they are easy to forget until finishes are already closing in on them.

scope.name: Enabling & site works
scope.desc: Clearance, utility diversions, access roads, the external works platform.

scope.name: Structure & envelope
scope.desc: Foundations, frame (steel or RC), roof and envelope — getting the building weather-tight.

scope.name: Internal partitions & finishes
scope.desc: Classroom/lab partitioning, ceilings, flooring and paint across many repeated room types.

scope.name: Mechanical (HVAC)
scope.desc: Ventilation and cooling serving classrooms, labs, halls and the kitchen/canteen.

scope.name: Electrical power & lighting
scope.desc: Power distribution and general + classroom lighting to the compliant lux level for teaching spaces.

scope.name: Fire & life safety
scope.desc: Detection, alarm, evacuation, sprinklers/hydrants and lockdown provisions for occupied classrooms.

scope.name: ELV / security / data
scope.desc: Access control, CCTV, structured cabling for classroom IT/AV, and the PA/bell system.

scope.name: Plumbing & sanitary
scope.desc: Toilets, ablution blocks and kitchen/canteen wet services.

scope.name: Testing, commissioning & handover
scope.desc: System testing, life-safety sign-off, IT/AV commissioning and handover in time for term start.

must_get_right: The handover date is fixed by the academic calendar, not negotiable — build the schedule backward from day one of term.
Life-safety (alarm, evacuation, lockdown) and IT/AV sign-off are what actually gate occupancy — protect them, not the structure.
Repeated room types (classrooms, labs) benefit from a typical-room finishing cycle — plan it like a repetitive floor, not one-off rooms.
Long-lead classroom furniture, AV equipment and specialist lab fixtures must be ordered early enough to land before finishes complete.

basis_of_planning.standard: AACE Recommended Practice 38R-06 — Documenting the Schedule Basis

sections.heading: Scheduling method & tools
sections.body: A Critical Path Method (CPM) network built in Primavera P6, developed to a Level 3 control schedule with retained-logic progress. Repeated classroom/lab room types are modelled as a typical-room finishing cycle so productivity assumptions are visible and auditable, not buried in one lump activity.

sections.heading: Calendars & working time
sections.body: Structure and MEP rough-in run a standard single- or two-shift working week; internal finishes and IT/AV fit-out move to extended hours in the final weeks to protect the fixed term-date handover. A weather allowance sits in the civil calendar where relevant.

sections.heading: Sequencing logic & critical path
sections.body: The driving path runs structure weather-tight → internal finishes & MEP rough-in across classroom wings as parallel repetitive fronts → life-safety commissioning → IT/AV fit-out and sign-off, all paced by the fixed academic-term start date rather than by any single technical bottleneck.

sections.heading: Key assumptions
sections.body: Design freeze on classroom/lab layouts, authority (civil defence/education) approvals obtained per phase, a single mobilisation, and classroom furniture/AV free-issue coordinated with the client. Any change to the term-date handover invalidates the baseline.

sections.heading: Access, resource & site constraints
sections.body: Repeated classroom and lab work benefits from a typical-room cycle so finishing trades move room-to-room at a set productivity rate. Skilled finishing trades are shared across many identical rooms and are a resource constraint late in the programme; site access may be constrained on urban plots with limited laydown.

sections.heading: Risks, float & contingency
sections.body: The fixed term-date handover is the primary risk driver, not a technical single-point-of-failure — schedule contingency is held immediately before life-safety and IT/AV sign-off rather than spread thinly across finishing activities. Late design changes to classroom layouts and authority inspection cycles are tracked risks.

sections.heading: Schedule levels of detail
sections.body: Reported at Level 1 (milestones) and Level 2 (summary) to the client; controlled at Level 3; expanded to Level 4–5 lookahead for the typical-room finishing cycle and commissioning — consistent with AACE 37R-06.
